newsitem.title: GERMANY: German shares in consolidative mode after new high.
newsitem.headline: German shares in consolidative mode after new high.

text.p: German shares, which ended bourse trade on Wednesday at a new record closing high, face a period of consolidation before the DAX index can gain fresh momentum to make a run at 3,900 points, traders say.
The 30-share DAX index ended bourse trade up 34.91 points at 3,854.76 points after reaching a new all-time high at 3,871.13 points at the outset of bourse dealings.
"The pretty strong dollar has really given this market a fresh outlook," said one Frankfurt trader who noted the dollar had traded above 1.75 marks in European dealings.
"The outlook for now is for a consolidative tone before making another attempt to go higher," the trader said.
Gains may also be limited due to cautious trading before the Federal Reserve releases the results of its FOMC policy meeting later on Wednesday.

The German market has found strength in recent days from investors taking a renewed interest in the chemical sector and Hoechst AG, which rose nearly six percent on Tuesday on fresh buy recommendations from some brokerage houses.
"The chemicals are still in demand this morning but they are due for some consolidation after Tuesday," said a trader.

Deutsche Morgan Grenfell said on Wednesday it had lowered some earnings estimates for Bayer and BASF AG and had reduced its earnings estimates for Hoechst for 1997 but had raised its estimates for Hoechst for 1998 and 1999.
The recommendation on all three of the major German chemical groups remained unchanged at "neutral" but with a higher weighting for Hoechst within the sector, DMG said.
Hoechst ended bourse trade up one mark at 79.30 marks, while BASF AG ended down one pfennig at 66.05 marks and Bayer AG was up 45 pfennigs at 70.75 marks.
Banking shares were also in the spotlight on Wednesday, in part due to the higher dollar, traders said.
Detusche Bank AG helped lead the advance and reached a new all-time high at 105.35 marks in bourse dealings. Deutsche shares ended bourse trade up 2.75 marks at 104.80 marks.
Rivals Commerzbank AG and Dresdner Bank AG were also higher, with Commerzbank up one mark at 50.15 marks and Dresdner up 1.35 pfennigs at 62.60 marks.
